quote: Were you able to see, like, an estimate and everything for your home?
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior visit where reps took measurements/photos and never followed up — a competitive and trust signal the rep never digs into (which company, what happened, why no follow-up).
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be intentionally moving past it quickly to get to qualifying questions rather than dwelling on a cold trail — but the call never returns to it, so no strategic payoff materializes.
coaching_implication: Ask a follow-up: 'who was that with, and did they ever explain why they didn't come back?' — this builds legitimacy contrast and rapport.

quote: What are your company Well, there's no no charge for that. Right?
stewart_read: Customer asking about cost/commitment after a long lapse is a live engagement signal — he's testing the offer, not rejecting it.
coaching_implication: Rep should have leaned into this spark with a confident no-obligation reassurance and then re-engaged the interest question, instead of stumbling through a vague answer.

stewart_read: Rep's response to the cost question is halting and unclear ('Well, let's... No... I I don't think... Yeah'), undermining the legitimacy reassurance right when the customer showed openness.
coaching_implication: Have a clean, rehearsed no-obligation line ready: 'Yep, totally free, no commitment at all — just gives you real numbers to look at.'

quote: I think it's gonna be hard for those solar panels to to work efficiently.
stewart_read: Rep disqualifies solely off a yes/no tree-presence answer with no follow-up on tree height, direction, roof orientation, or whether the customer would consider trimming before ending pursuit.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be a legitimate hard-gate DQ if the trees genuinely block southern exposure entirely, but the transcript shows no exploration to confirm that severity before closing the call.
coaching_implication: Ask clarifying questions (which side of the roof, how tall, would you consider removal) before disqualifying — shade DQs should be confirmed, not assumed from a single yes.

quote: yeah. If you ever plan on cutting those down or anything, just feel free to reach out, and we'd love to help you out.
stewart_read: Call ends with a vague open-door offer and no ownership of a next step, no verify completion, no bill capture, and no explicit handshake.
coaching_implication: Even on a probable DQ, rep should confirm whether trimming is realistically planned and set a concrete follow-up window rather than leaving it fully open-ended.

quote: So this is Holland with Ion. I got a request you were looking into solar for your home.
stewart_read: Intro references the lead request but skips any company/legitimacy anchor beyond the name, which becomes relevant once the customer questions cost/commitment 40 seconds later.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer's 'Good' response and continued cooperation suggests the light intro was sufficient for this call, so this may be a minor rather than consequential omission.
coaching_implication: A stronger open ('certified solar installer' framing) could have preempted the customer's legitimacy question altogether.
